To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dual inducer signal recognition of an ROK family member, VC2007 in Vibrio cholera, has been achieved by the evolution of two independent inducer recognition sites in a single protein.
the ROK protein, Mlc, is a dual inducer sensor that can respond to either glucose (via interaction with PtsG) or N-acetylglucose (GlcNA) (via interaction with GlcNAc transporter, NagE).
the Mlc homologue in Vibrio cholera has evolved the ability to sense two different inducers: the dephospho form of the GlcNAcin-specific transporter, and GlcNA6P.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of regulation of gene expression in bacteria.
the regulation of gene expression in response to nutrient availability.
understanding how bacteria sense and respond to environmental stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ROK family of transcription factors has evolved a dual inducer signal recognition mechanism.
the ROK proteins are dual inducer sensors, with the ability to recognize two different inducer molecules, and that this ability has evolved by the recruitment of different domains to the ROK core.
the dual inducer recognition of the NagC homologue VC2007 is a consequence of the evolutionary divergence of the NagC family from the Mlc family, and the evolutionary divergence of VC2007 from Mlc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mlc homologues in E. coli and V. cholerae are able to recognize two different signals, glucose and GlcNac respectively, but the mechanism of signal recognition has been conserved.
we have shown that the Mlc family of proteins have evolved to sense different categories of inducers, which in turn have different effects on the expression of target genes.

the ROK family of proteins has evolved from a single ancestral protein, which responded to the phosphorylated sugar, Glc6P, to a family of proteins, each of which has evolved to respond to different inducers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dual inducer sensing by VC2007, a Mlc paralogue, is a consequence of the evolution of two independent signals that are recognized by different regions of the protein.
, in addition to glucose, the ROK family can sense GlcNAc, and that sensing of GlcNAc is achieved by the ROK protein binding to a specific inducer, the GlcNAG transporter.
, although the ROK family proteins are highly similar in sequence and share a conserved mechanism of action, they can be adapted to respond to different signals.
